summary: Sucre stands under the national framework of Colombia. No Sucre-specific signal was identified in the source inventory, and the national assessment applies.
tangentialFactors:
The reporting available for this record consists of national investigations whose documented incidents occurred in other departments, notably Antioquia and Caquetá. Their counts are raw national totals with no per-capita or population denominator, so they establish a country-wide pattern of targeted killings and displacement rather than any rate attributable to Sucre.

The same sources record that the Attorney General's Office does not classify killings of trans women as transfemicide, logging them as ordinary cases, and that armed groups circulate 'social cleansing' flyers naming trans women for death. Whether either practice operates inside Sucre is not addressed by any source consulted.
localsOnly: No resident-facing facts specific to Sucre were sourced: local police practice, local notary or registry handling of gender-marker changes, and local health-service access for trans residents are all unsourced for this department.
outOfScopeNotes:
Unresolved: whether armed-group threat campaigns, forced displacement of trans women, or killings of trans people have been recorded in Sucre at any date. No source in the inventory covers the department.

Unresolved: how prosecutors in Sucre classify the killing of a trans woman, and whether the national practice of recording such deaths as ordinary cases rather than transfemicide is followed locally. Not sourced for this department.
